messages.subject: multi_normal distribution for multivarite posterior
parts:
Hi to all, I now have some troubles with multivariate normal distribution (while I tried to carrefully read the manual).
with:   
> vector[2] mu;
in the model block, how can I declare something like (which doesn't work):

for (n in 1:N)
   y[n] ~ multi_normal(mu,sigma);
  mu[1] <- a*X+b
  mu[2] <- c*X+d
}

both lines mu[1] and mu[2] are the issues.
Thank you.

- Leon-Alph

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multi_normal distribution for multivarite  posterior
parts:
You need a semicolon at end of each line. Also I think you need to define
mu before it is used in the expression for y, not after, as Stan code is
executed sequentially.

> Hi to all, I now have some troubles with multivariate normal distribution
> (while I tried to carrefully read the manual).
> with:
>> vector[2] mu;
> in the model block, how can I declare something like (which doesn't work):
>
> for (n in 1:N)
> y[n] ~ multi_normal(mu,sigma);
> mu[1] <- a*X+b
> mu[2] <- c*X+d
> }
>
> both lines mu[1] and mu[2] are the issues.
> Thank you.
>
> - Leon-Alph
>

Thank you.
I forgot the semicolon when I reproduced my code, and I didn't pay attention to the order.
Other question:
If it's sequential, when a model looks like:

model{
      X[i] ~ normal(a*X+c,sigma);
     Y[i] ~ normal(a*Y+b,sigma);
}

The estimation of the shared parameter "a" takes into accound both lines or only the second one (as it's sequential) ?
note: I know I could write this model with vectors but mine includes polynomial division and so doesn't support linear algebra rewritting.
